property_summary: For any caller address, only the admin (the deployer) can change C.owner via setOwner in the reference; the mutant that removes the onlyAdmin check allows some non-admin caller to successfully change owner, breaking this rule.

For any caller address provided by the fuzz harness, when the admin calls setOwner(_owner) the contract's public owner must equal the provided _owner; the mutant that sets owner = tx.origin breaks this because tx.origin may differ from the supplied _owner for some inputs.

For any admin caller and any address _owner passed to setOwner, the correct contract sets owner() equal to the provided _owner after the call; the mutant that uses tx.origin instead can produce a different owner when the admin is a contract (tx.origin != the provided _owner), so the rule is violated for some inputs.

For any admin caller and any target address _owner, when the admin calls setOwner(_owner) the contract's owner() equals the supplied _owner; the mutant that assigns owner = tx.origin can break this when the admin is a contract (tx.origin != _owner).

For every admin caller A and any address newOwner, when A (the admin) calls setOwner(newOwner) the contract's owner() becomes exactly newOwner; the mutant that writes owner = tx.origin can make owner() differ (e.g., when the admin is a contract and tx.origin != newOwner).

For any admin caller and any fuzzed address newOwner, when the admin calls setOwner(newOwner) the contract's owner() equals the supplied newOwner; the mutant that assigns owner = tx.origin can make owner() differ (e.g. when the admin is a contract), so the property is violated for some inputs.

For any address provided to setOwner by the admin, the contract's owner getter equals that provided address after the call; the mutant that assigns address(0) breaks this because owner will be address(0) instead of the provided address for some inputs.

Rule: only the admin (the deployer) can successfully call setOwner and change owner; the mutant inverts the check allowing non-admins to change owner, so there exist callers for which owner differs after setOwner between reference and mutant.

For any caller and any address argument, calling setOwner(...) from the admin always returns true (the reference guarantees a true success return); the mutant returns false for some inputs, violating this return-value property.

For all callers, only the admin (the account that deployed C) can successfully call setOwner (i.e., calls by non-admins revert); the mutant removes the admin check so some non-admin callers will succeed, violating this rule.

For any address newOwner, calling setOwner(newOwner) as the admin always updates the public owner variable to newOwner in the reference; the mutant instead updates admin so the public owner sometimes differs from newOwner.

For every caller and input, only the original admin (the deployer) can successfully call setOwner; the mutant allowing owner to act as admin breaks this by enabling some other caller (the current owner) to succeed where the admin-only rule should prevent it.

For all callers, only the original admin (the deployer) may successfully call setOwner; the mutant lets the current owner (a different address) call setOwner and thus allows a non-admin caller to succeed for some inputs.
